job: Read one customer's story of moving to the product, as an article with its evidence.
purpose: A customer story on Ember's public site: Quarry Labs moving 14 scrapers to Ember. A title on a picture (the image ground) with the spend chart set across the page under it, then a narrow reading column (fd-prose, one picture as a figure) broken by a proof quote, the four steps of the move with the code each one used, one large figure and two pull quotes, ending with more stories. It reads like an article: no logos, no pricing, no call-to-action band.
useWhen: A customer's change is worth telling at reading length, with figures they agree to publish.
The page links from a quote on the home or from the changelog.

avoidWhen.when: The page sells the product to someone new to it.
The page explains how to do the task, step by step.
The page lists many posts or releases.

sections.why: An editorial page: the links centred like a magazine's masthead.
A story opens on a picture, as a magazine's does; its evidence (the spend chart) follows across the page.
The reading column the other sections break; one fd-site-media figure (paper) in it.
The head of data's words beside the one figure the story turns on.
Each step of the move is a split of its own: the text beside the call that replaced a scraper.
One figure carries this part of the story, with the sentence that says what it counts.
Two pull quotes from the people the change reached.
The next story large, three more beside it.
After an article the reader looks for somewhere to go next.

states.name: menu open
states.how: below 900px wide, the header's menu button opens the links as a sheet (data-state="open")
